newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Traded down with active bids/offers.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Traded down with active bids/offers.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices slipped on Thursday in active trade, with some traders saying that a local trading company was pricing the market.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $98.50 per tonne and the 380-cst was done at $96 per tonne, traders said.
A local trader bought both cargoes from two majors.
The 180-cst was last traded at $101.50 per tonne on Monday.
"The spread is just too low... It's very apparent the local trader is trying to price the market," said one trader.
The local company and its sister company together bought seven cargoes so far since last week.
Traders said the two trading firms were likely buying for Indonesia where some refinery units will be shut down in July for maintenance.
"I think their buying will continue for a while," said another trader.
Traders said Indonesia's state oil firm Pertamina has initially decided to allocate 2.3 million barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for July but details were not yet available.
Pertamina allocated 3.1 million barrels in June, with additional 500,000 barrels rolled over from May.
A Japanese trader said he saw prices at above 80-90 cents per barrel over the Pertamina formula.
"Supplies will be very tight in July," said one trader.
On the SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, July was traded $1 down to $100, with 55 100-tonne lots traded.
